map.An equation is a rule for computing the: An equation is a rule. It finds the dependent variable from the independent one. Test a rule on every row of the table. One lucky row proves nothing.
Now the main line. Hours in, liters out. Find its rule. Then we know how thirsty this dome is.
Fill in the table. Then write the rule. Each row is proof.

map.Conceptual: the table hides one rule — e: Conceptual: the table hides one rule. Each y comes from its x the SAME way. This is true in every row. A rule that fits one row is luck. It is not a rule.
map.Procedural: compare each pair: 1 → 4, 2: Procedural: compare each pair: 1 → 4, 2 → 8, 3 → 12. Is y always the same MULTIPLE of its x? Find the multiplier with row one. Check it on rows two and three. Then use it at x = 5.

map.A coordinate pair (x, y) marks one momen: A coordinate pair is (x, y). It marks one moment of a relationship. x = the independent value. y = the dependent value. Order matters.

map.Found our villain. No mastermind — just: Found our bad guy. Not a big boss. Just a rusty controller. Look at the wires.
map.It's been reading temperature as the INP: It reads heat as the INPUT. It reads fan time as the OUTPUT. It wired cause and effect the wrong way.
map.Confirmed. It swapped the independent an: Yes. It swapped the independent and dependent variables. For years the dome bossed the heat gauge. It obeyed the fans. So sad.
